g.title:
4. Bank Primary Data Center — Lagos (Equinix / MainOne Tier III) [Core On-Premises Tier] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: The bank's central on-premises computing facility housing Infosys Finacle 11.x Core Banking, on-prem Core Banking Middleware JBoss cluster, Oracle Database 19c Enterprise RAC (2-Node), local Active Data Guard query replica, Dell EMC Data Domain (DD6900), Interswitch Postilion Switch, and self-hosted ERP/Treasury applications.
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Serves as the ultimate system of record and financial transaction settlement core. Authorizes double-entry general ledger entries, settles interbank payments, issues debit cards, and anchors the bank's regulatory book of accounts.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: Huawei Cloud Hybrid Gateway via 1 Gbps Direct Connect MPLS (mTLS Port 443), Branch SD-WAN Routers via IPsec (Ports 8000-8080), Payment Switches via ISO 8583 (Port 9000) • OUTBOUND: Secondary DR DC via Active Data Guard (Port 1521 over DCI Dark Fiber), Databricks Lakehouse via GoldenGate CDC (Port 9092), Secondary Data Domain via DD Boost (Port 2051) • FAILOVER: Active-Active 2-node Oracle RAC with ASM, redundant power, Dell VxRail HCI vSAN, and dual-homed telecom feeds. • SECURITY: Thales payShield 10K hardware HSM for PIN translation, Oracle TDE encryption with hardware keys, Fortinet NGFW perimeter, and physical biometric mantrap access. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: 4. BANK PRIMARY DATA CENTER — LAGOS (EQUINIX / MAINONE TIER III COLOCATION)

g.title:
Core Banking Middleware Bus (On-Prem Primary DC) [Section 4] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: Enterprise Service Bus (Red Hat JBoss EAP / OSB) cluster hosting Account Core Service, Identity Core Service, Payment Core Service, Card Core Service, and on-prem Apache Kafka backbone.
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Acts as the central integration and protocol translation layer between Huawei Cloud digital microservices and Infosys Finacle core banking. Translates external REST/JSON into internal FIXML/EJB requests.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: Huawei Cloud Hybrid Gateway via 1 Gbps Direct Connect MPLS (mTLS TCP 443) • OUTBOUND: Infosys Finacle Core Banking Engine via high-speed gigabit LAN (FIXML / EJB Ports 9080-9085) • FAILOVER: Active-Active clustered deployment across Dell VxRail HCI nodes with automated session failover. • SECURITY: Mutual TLS (mTLS) with internal PKI certificates, Thales payShield 10K HSM, and PAM database credentials. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: CORE BANKING MIDDLEWARE BUS (ON-PREM PRIMARY DC)
Enterprise Service Bus (Red Hat JBoss / OSB)
• Bridges Huawei Cloud digital microservices to Finacle
• Protocol translation: REST/JSON to Finacle ISO/FIXML
Balance inquiry, mini-statement, account holds, limits
Direct synchronous call to Finacle Core Banking Engine
Customer Information File (CIF) management & KYC tiers
Integrates with NIMC, BVN and biometric enrolment desks
Two-phase commit coordinator for interbank payments
Card transaction authorization & ISO 8583 message bridge
Card account balance inquiry & stand-in processing
Local event streaming cluster for transaction journals
MirrorMaker 2 replication to Cloud DMS Kafka
• Direct Connect Ingress: Strict IP whitelisting & mTLS client certificates
• Thales payShield 10K HSM for PIN block translation & MACing
• Delinea Secret Server for database credential management
• Active-Active clustered deployment across Dell VxRail HCI nodes

g.title:
Infosys Finacle Core Banking System (11.x) [Section 4: Primary Data Center] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: Tier-1 enterprise core banking engine running on Red Hat Enterprise Linux across high-spec Dell PowerEdge compute nodes.
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: The primary operational heartbeat of the bank. Maintains the double-entry Chart of Accounts, executes deposits, withdrawals, loan repayments, trade finance, and end-of-day (EOD) general ledger balancing.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: Core Middleware Bus via FIXML / EJB (Ports 9080-9085), Branch Tellering Desks via SD-WAN • OUTBOUND: Primary Oracle 19c RAC Master via Oracle Net (Port 1521), Postilion Switch via ISO 8583 (Port 9000) • FAILOVER: Dell VxRail hypervisor clustering; disaster recovery failover to Secondary DC Finacle Standby via VMware SRM runbooks. • SECURITY: Strict dual-control authorization (maker-checker), encrypted EJB transport, database connection pooling with PAM credentials, and annual PCI-DSS audit. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: Tier-1 Core Banking Platform running on Red Hat Enterprise Linux:
• General Ledger & Chart of Accounts: Multi-currency, multi-branch ledger
• Deposit & Lending Engines: CASA, Term Deposits, Overdrafts, Loans
• Trade Finance & FX: Letters of Credit, Bank Guarantees, FX Cash/Spot
• End-of-Day (EOD) Batch Engine: Automated interest, accruals & GL balancing

g.title:
Postilion Realtime Financial Switch [Section 4: Primary Data Center] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: High-throughput electronic payment switching engine backed by Microsoft SQL Server AlwaysOn Availability Groups.
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Routes, validates, and switches ATM, POS, and online card payments. Translates ISO 8583 transactions, interfaces with Thales payShield HSM for PIN verification, and routes interbank payments to NIBSS NIP and Interswitch.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: ATM Fleet & POS Terminals via ISO 8583 (Port 9000), Digital Card Microservices via ISO Bridge • OUTBOUND: NIBSS Instant Payments (NIP) via Dedicated MPLS (Ports 9000-9100), Interswitch Gateway via Cross-Connect (Ports 9000-9100), Thales payShield HSM (Port 1500) • FAILOVER: AlwaysOn High Availability Group across Primary and DR Data Centers with sub-second failover. • SECURITY: Hardware HSM MAC generation and PIN translation, DUKPT remote key management, and PCI-DSS certification. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: • ISO 8583 financial switching engine for ATM, POS & Web acquiring
• Direct links to NIBSS Instant Payments (NIP) & Interswitch Verve
• Backed by Microsoft SQL Server AlwaysOn Availability Groups
• ISO 20022 MX Messaging & Legacy MT103/MT202 wires
• Dedicated Hardware HSM & Air-Gapped CSCF Enclave

g.title:
Self-Hosted Enterprise Applications (Dell VxRail) [Section 4: Primary Data Center] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: Mission-critical enterprise resource planning (SAP S/4HANA Finance), capital markets treasury (Finacle Treasury & Calypso), automated fraud reconciliation (Fiserv E-Match/X-Match), business process workflows (K2 BPM), biometric staff payroll (Softworks HRMS), and software robots (Blue Prism RPA).
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Executes double-entry general ledger accounting, automated interbank reconciliation, tax remittances, digital credit origination workflows, and robotic process automation across bank operations. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)

g.text: Financial accounting, vendor procurement, fixed assets (SAP SE)
Fixed income, money markets, FX dealing, Bloomberg B-PIPE link
Automated transaction reconciliation & AML enterprise fraud detection
Digital credit appraisal, expense approvals, account modification
Staff payroll calculation, tax remittances, leaves, biometrics
Software bots for automated statements, NACS, and reconciliations

g.title:
Oracle Database 19c Enterprise RAC (2-Node Cluster) [Section 4: Primary Data Center] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: Mission-critical active-active clustered relational database running on Oracle Grid Infrastructure and Automatic Storage Management (ASM).
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Stores the central ledger of record, account master tables, and transactional journals. Delivers continuous uptime, transactional ACID guarantees, and sub-millisecond write latency backed by Pure Storage NVMe SAN.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: Infosys Finacle Core Banking Engines via Oracle Net (Port 1521) • OUTBOUND: Secondary DR DC Oracle Standby via Active Data Guard (Port 1521 over DCI Dark Fiber), Databricks Delta Lake Bronze via GoldenGate CDC (Port 9092), Dell Data Domain via RMAN DD Boost (Port 2051) • FAILOVER: Active-Active 2-node clustering with transparent application failover (TAF); synchronous zero-loss Active Data Guard failover to DR DC (RPO=0, RTO<5 min). • SECURITY: Oracle Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) with keys managed in Thales payShield HSM, Oracle Database Vault separation of duties, and ACS 24/7 premium OEM support. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: • FlashArray//X All-NVMe SAN Storage (Sub-millisecond write latency)
• Vendor & OEM Support: Oracle Systems (ACS 24/7 Premium)

g.title:
Local Read-Only Query Replica (Active Data Guard) [Section 4: Primary Data Center] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: Dedicated read-only Oracle Active Data Guard instance deployed on-premises in the Primary Data Center with Real-Time Redo Apply.
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Protects transactional RAC nodes from locking and CPU exhaustion by offloading heavy financial reporting queries, audit investigations, and End-of-Day (EOD) balance extractions.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: Synchronized continuously from Primary RAC Master via Redo Transport (Port 1521) • OUTBOUND: Internal Reporting Tools, Financial Control & Compliance Desks via SQL*Net (Port 1521) • FAILOVER: Automatic real-time catch-up; zero impact on primary database availability. • SECURITY: Read-only database session enforcement; TDE hardware decryption. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: Local Read-Only Query Replica (Active Data Guard)
Local DC read query offload for reporting & EOD batch extraction:
• Active Data Guard Read-Only with Real-Time Apply (zero lag)
• Offloads heavy audit queries, financial control & EOD report generation
• Protects transactional RAC nodes from heavy analytics locks

g.title:
Dell EMC Data Domain (DD6900 Appliance) [Section 4: Primary Data Center] ================================================================================ 1. WHAT IT DOES: Enterprise deduplicating backup storage appliance integrated with Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) via Dell DD Boost.
2. ROLE IN WHOLE ARCHITECTURE: Captures hourly transactional archive logs and daily cumulative incremental RMAN database backups with >25:1 deduplication, replicating backup sets to DR Data Domain and writing to LTO-8 tapes.
3. HOW IT CONNECTS TO OTHERS: • INBOUND: Oracle 19c RAC and Virtual Machines via DD Boost (TCP Port 2051) • OUTBOUND: Secondary DR Data Domain via Asynchronous Encrypted WAN Replication, Dell PowerVault LTO-8 Tape Library for Montgomery Vaults Archival • FAILOVER: Dual controller redundancy; replicated backup catalog in DR facility. • SECURITY: DD Boost Kerberos authentication, retention lock immutability protecting against ransomware, and hardware AES-256 encryption. (Click box on diagram for interactive detail view)
g.text: • Oracle RMAN with DD Boost: Hourly archive logs & daily cumulative backups
• Deduplication ratio > 25:1 reducing storage and replication footprint
• Direct replication over DCI fiber to Secondary DR Data Domain
• Automated writes to PowerVault LTO-8 tape library
• Dell PowerEdge nodes running VMware vSphere Enterprise Plus
• VMware vSAN All-Flash storage & NSX-T Software Defined Networking
• Hosts Finacle Middleware, SAP ERP, Fiserv E-Match, and Postilion
• Thales payShield 10K hardware HSM for cryptographic keys & PIN blocks
• Oracle TDE (Transparent Data Encryption) with auto-rotating HSM keys
• CyberSOC Africa continuous syslog ingestion for SIEM correlation
